key_insight: SrTiO3-xHx oxyhydrides strongly prefer a cis O4H2 anion arrangement, and this ordering is highly sensitive to the DFT+U choice used to model Ti 3d reduction.
engineering_relevance: Accurate prediction of hydride ordering in perovskite oxyhydrides requires calibrated electronic-structure settings, since the wrong U value can shift stability by ~100 meV/anion and mislead materials design.
method: Built a cluster expansion for SrTiO3-xHx using HSE06 hybrid-DFT energetics.
Benchmarked DFT+U against HSE06 and identified U = 3.3 eV as an HSE06 proxy.
Used ground-state searches and Monte Carlo sampling to test anion-ordering trends and structural stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~100 meV/anion variation in mixing energies across DFT+U choices and ~200 meV per hydride stabilization for the cis configuration, consistent across ground states, correlations, and MC sampling.
watch_item: The ordering conclusions depend on the chosen U calibration and limited HSE06 training data, so transferability to other oxyhydrides or compositions may require revalidation.
paper_title: Long- and Short-Range Anion Order in SrTiO$_{3-x}$H$_x$ Perovskite Oxyhydrides: DFT+$U$ Sensitivity and HSE06 Cluster Expansion
